worker_corpus_quality.contract: Output strings hashed with UTF-8 and exact errors/IDs/order compared to same-platform W5; raw response bytes retained gzip per bounded batch. Native hash differences are not silently repinned. No timings measured.

binaryen_experiment.contract: Only standard -O3 with the pinned worker-build feature list, retained names/target features. No all-features, fast-math, ignore-implicit-traps or traps-never-happen. Not a runtime speed measurement.

cpu_affinity.reason: Hybrid CPU and observed unrelated background load. Pin single-thread API samples to the same performance core; retain normal priority. Multi-thread samples use all logical processors. User processes are not modified.

timing.contract: Rotated independent-process variant order; workload order reverses on alternate process rounds. First calls excluded from mean/median summaries, retained in raw rows. All accepted baseline output hashes enforced on every result. Unique removes byte-identical payload duplicates before API, so its speedup cannot be due to batch duplicate sharing. No input/filesystem cold-cache claim. Process peak working set includes loading, verification and retained results; not heap payload. Optional prewarm runs are archived separately and were declared before the cohort. Instrumented timing is diagnostic only and must not be used as performance evidence.

limitations: Allocation/profile/quality runs overlap builds and other validation. None of their elapsed times or RSS values are speed evidence.
Whole API request totals include request-local sharing; the fresh phase workload differs. Compare within each workload contract.
A 10.44% request reduction from W5 is not a 10.44% speed gain. Peak requested payload on the all-input run increases by 5520 bytes.
Reconstruction retains at most 64KiB of decoded-line vector capacity per active scope; larger inputs stay eager. Counter byte totals are cumulative, not simultaneous retained heap.

Four balanced independent-process rounds, eight repeated corpus samples and 80 named-script samples. First calls/prewarm are retained separately. All owned builds, tests, scans and source edits were idle throughout timing.

All ten declared workload means improve versus the original baseline. This cohort has no W6 control; it cannot establish the incremental speed contribution of W7 alone or be multiplied with earlier cohorts.
Eight corpus samples make nearest-rank p95 the maximum, not a precise population-tail estimate. RSS is whole-process working set, not Rust live payload; several workloads have small RSS increases.

All 3978 results match between Wasm W5/W7/W7+Binaryen, including 42 empty-input errors. 142 preexisting Wasm/native successful-source differences persist identically; their semantic equivalence was not independently established here.
PGO, Binaryen and cache ablations are separate experiments, not default promotion or assigned speedups before their timing gates.
